title: Stable Response Frames, Error Semantics, and Tool Handoff Acceptance Criteria (PRD)
creator: Maya Chen
description: This PRD defines agreement-level acceptance criteria for streamed structured responses that may include function/tool invocations. It standardizes framing (how partial JSON pieces are emitted), deterministic error semantics, handshake and retry behavior for tool handoffs, and the observability signals required for safe rollouts. Goal: ensure consumer applications can dependably parse, resume, and reconcile partially emitted outputs across network interruptions and model fallbacks.
background: Multiple customers have reported inconsistent behavior when using streamed structured responses that include tool calls: partial objects without clear delimiters, ambiguous failure states for invoked tools, and difficulty reconciling partial state after reconnects. Existing Linear tickets contain scattered acceptance checks for streaming and tool-calling; this ticket consolidates the contract-level requirements and defines testable acceptance criteria and observability needs.
goals: Define a minimal, versioned frame format for streamed structured responses that supports partial object emission, checkpointing, and explicit completion/abandonment markers.
Specify deterministic error states for tool calls invoked during a stream (success / tool-error / transient / aborted) and required metadata to make retries idempotent.
Ensure clear fallback semantics when the primary model or dedicated capacity falls back to a different model variant (preserve partial outputs, continue vs restart behavior).
Provide an observable surface (events/metrics/logs) to detect and alert on schema violations, fragmented objects, and tool-handshake failures.
Deliver an acceptance test harness with synthetic workloads and a set of golden transcripts to validate behavior across reconnects, backpressure, and tool restarts.
non_goals: Mandating a single high-level JSON schema for all customers — this ticket defines framing + semantics, not domain schemas.
Implementing full retry orchestration for third-party tools (we only specify idempotency tokens and recommended retry guidance).
Reworking the entire SDK surface — SDK changes will be follow-ups tracked in sub-issues.
acceptance_criteria: Frame format: every streamed emission MUST be one of: 'FRAME.partial', 'FRAME.checkpoint', or 'FRAME.done'. Each frame includes 'frame_id' (uuid), 'schema_version' (semver string), and 'cursor' (monotonic integer).

Partial object emission: Partial frames may contain 'fragment' (string) and 'path' (dot-delimited path into the final JSON). Consumer can reconstruct full object by applying fragments in cursor order; framing guarantees no overlapping fragments for the same path without an intervening checkpoint.

Checkpoint semantics: 'FRAME.checkpoint' signals a durable reconciliation point. Once a checkpoint is emitted for cursor N, the system guarantees that replays starting at N will not re-emit prior fragments for the same path unless explicit 'FRAME.override' is used (see below).

Completion: 'FRAME.done' includes final status: 'ok'|'partial_ok'|'failed' and a canonical 'result_digest' (sha256) for final output when available. Consumers must be able to treat 'partial_ok' as acceptable for use-cases that tolerate partial results.

Tool invocation handshake: Tool calls must be represented in-stream as 'TOOL.invocation' frames containing 'tool_id', 'call_id' (uuid), 'idempotency_key' (optional per-caller), and 'intent_schema' (reference). The runtime must emit a corresponding 'TOOL.outcome' frame with statuses: 'succeeded','tool_error','transient_error','cancelled'.

Idempotency and replay: If a stream reconnects and the runtime finds an existing 'call_id' with a matching 'idempotency_key', it MUST not re-invoke the external tool; it MUST re-emit the previously recorded 'TOOL.outcome' frame instead.

Failure modes defined: 'tool_error' (deterministic failure from tool; includes 'error_code' and 'human_message'), 'transient_error' (retryable; runtime may attempt N retry attempts where N <= configured_retry_limit), and 'cancelled' (explicit cancellation from consumer or runtime).

Backpressure and pacing: When the consumer signals 'FLOW.pause' with a reason and optional timeout, the runtime must stop emitting new 'TOOL.invocation' frames beyond already-started calls; already in-flight tool calls may complete and emit outcome frames. Resume must be explicitly signaled with 'FLOW.resume'.

Fallback semantics: When the runtime routes to a fallback model variant mid-stream, it must emit 'ROUTE.change' frame containing prior cursor and a 'continuation_policy' field with values: 'continue', 'restart', or 'truncate'. The fallback policy is chosen according to routing tier; acceptance tests must validate at least 'continue' and 'restart'.

Schema violations: If a frame fails basic framing validation (missing frame_id/schema_version/cursor), runtime must emit a 'FRAME.error' with 'severity' (warning|fatal). 'fatal' causes stream termination with 'FRAME.done' status 'failed'.

Observability: For every stream we must emit structured telemetry events (traceable by stream_id): 'stream.start','frame.emitted','tool.invoked','tool.outcome','frame.checkpoint','stream.done','frame.error'. Each event includes stream_id, cursor, model_variant, region, and latency_ms (for frame roundtrip).
Telemetry SLAs: The platform must surface a console dashboard that counts schema violations per 1000 streams and alert when rate exceeds 0.5% over a 30m window.

Test harness: Provide automated tests that validate reconstruction of partial objects after simulated disconnects (0–3 reconnects), verify idempotency behavior for tool calls, validate backpressure signals, and confirm correct 'ROUTE.change' policies. Golden transcripts (at least 8 scenarios) must be included.
test_plan: Integration tests: 8 golden transcripts executed in the CI pipeline (normal success, tool transient error with retry, tool deterministic failure, reconnect after checkpoint, reconnect before checkpoint, fallback 'continue', fallback 'restart', backpressure pause/resume).
Chaos test: 24-hour load test injecting random disconnects and tool latencies; measure percent of streams with successful reconstruction >= 99.5%.
Manual review: PM + Eng + DX review of SDK parsing examples and sample app before release.
metrics: tool.idempotency_mismatch_rate <= 0.01% (cases where idempotency_key did not prevent duplicate tool invocation)
mean_time_to_frame_emit < 50ms under p95 load for frames without tool-invocations
rollout_plan: Canary: enable framing v1 for 1% of hosted API traffic with strict logging + debug traces for 24 hours.
Validation: run golden transcripts against canary traffic and verify telemetry thresholds.
Gradual ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over multi-day windows with rollback gates at each step if customer-facing errors or schema_violation_rate exceed thresholds.
Dedicated customers: opt-in earlier via feature flag and coordinated migration guide.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Consumers with naive parsers may fail on partial frames. Mitigation: publish SDK helpers and example parsers; include compatibility test cases.
Risk: Third-party tools with non-idempotent operations may produce duplicate side-effects. Mitigation: require idempotency_key guidance and recommend storing call outcomes on tool side when possible.
Risk: Increased telemetry volume. Mitigation: sample non-error streams at 1% while retaining all error traces.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates framing/versioning concerns from domain-level schema evolution. The schema_version field allows independent evolution of domain schemas.
A follow-up PM ticket will define SDK changes and migration docs once runtime v1 framing is stabilized.
